clinical_course: Presented with 2-day history of polyuria, polydipsia and vomiting; found to be in DKA with glucose 468 mg/dL, pH 7.18, ketones 4+. Managed on IV insulin infusion and fluid/electrolyte replacement per protocol for 36h, anion gap closed by day 2. Transitioned to subcutaneous basal-bolus insulin on day 3, tolerating oral intake, blood glucose stable 110-180 mg/dL on discharge regimen. Diabetes educator reviewed insulin technique, hypoglycemia recognition and sick-day rules with patient and family before discharge.
follow_up: Endocrinology OPD review in 5 days with home glucose log. Repeat HbA1c and TSH/anti-TPO at 3 months. Contact clinic if unable to reach target glucose despite correct dosing.
warning_signs: Blood glucose below 70 mg/dL with symptoms not relieved by juice/glucose tablets, repeated vomiting, fruity breath odor, confusion, breathing difficulty, or inability to keep fluids down.
activity_and_diet: Diabetic diet as counseled by dietitian, consistent carbohydrate intake at meals. Normal activity as tolerated; carry a fast-acting glucose source at all times.

medications.name: insulin aspart
medications.frequency: before each meal per sliding scale

medications.name: ondansetron
medications.frequency: every 8 hours as needed for nausea
